name: skewed join (one hot key dominates a join side)
symptom: one straggler task in the join stage while other tasks finish in ms; job hangs at 99% with few tasks left
detection in plan or UI or event log: Spark UI stage detail: max task duration >> median (event log: stage max_ms vs p50_ms); plan shows SortMergeJoin on the skewed key
fix: enable AQE skew join (on by default in 3.2+: "Spark dynamically handles skew in sort-merge join by splitting (and replicating if needed) skewed partitions" - docs); or manual key salting; or two-phase aggregation for skewed groupBy
how to measure the saving: compare stage max/p50 task runtime and job wall time before/after; both visible in event log or UI
measured effect: stage 4661ms straggler vs p50 255ms (18x, 8 tasks) with AQE off; wall 5.85s. With AQE on (advisory 128KB, skew threshold 256KB to match the small demo data): 6 balanced tasks, wall 2.2s. Manual salting: 4.52s. [local, e02, runs/e02_*/summary.json]
risks: AQE defaults (64MB advisory, 256MB skew threshold) target cluster-scale data - they did nothing on a 1.8MB demo shuffle until lowered; salting adds a shuffle and code complexity
prerequisites: AQE: spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true + skewJoin.enabled=true; local Spark 3.5.6 (defaults probed in runs/defaults_probe.txt)

name: wrong shuffle partition count (too few or too many)
symptom: too few: cores idle, long tasks, possible OOM; too many: thousands of tiny tasks, scheduling overhead, small files on write
detection in plan or UI or event log: stage task count equals spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default 200, probed locally); UI shows many sub-ms tasks (too many) or task count < cores (too few)
fix: set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions per job ~ total shuffle bytes / (2-4x cores x exec.memory guidance is folklore; practical rule: 100-200MB per partition, folklore label); or rely on AQE coalescing ("You do not need to set a proper shuffle partition number to fit your dataset" - docs)
how to measure the saving: wall time + per-stage task count from event log for several values
measured effect: 4M-row groupBy on local[4]: sp=4 1.43s, sp=16 1.13s, sp=200 1.32s, sp=1000 2.48s (2.2x spread; 1000 partitions = 1000 tasks of 3ms median). [local, e03]
risks: fixed value wrong for every job; AQE coalescing handles the "too many" side only
prerequisites: initial partitions large enough: spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.initialPartitionNum

name: AQE disabled (or AQE thresholds mis-set for data size)
symptom: static plan used even when runtime stats prove it wrong: wrong join strategy, un-coalesced partitions, un-split skew
detection in plan or UI or event log: final plan (explain formatted after execution, or SQL tab in UI) lacks "AdaptiveSparkPlan isFinalPlan=true" and post-shuffle changes; on Databricks blog: gains came "from dynamic partition coalescing and dynamic join strategy switching"
fix: enable spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=true (default since 3.2.0 per docs); check coalescePartitions/skewJoin subflags; verify thresholds vs actual shuffle sizes
how to measure the saving: wall time before/after; count join-strategy conversions in final plan
measured effect: AQE off 0.99s/200 tasks vs on 0.31s/1 task for a 20-group aggregation (3.2x). Blog: "Adaptive Query Execution yielded up to an 8x speedup" on TPC-DS, "32 queries had more than 1.1x speedup". [local e04 + blog]
risks: plan changes between runs (harder debugging); skew thresholds tuned for big data do nothing on small shuffles (measured: had to lower advisory 64MB->128KB to demo)
prerequisites: Spark 3.2+

name: small files (many tiny Parquet/Delta/Iceberg files)
symptom: slow scans, huge job setup, driver metadata pressure, "too many files" listing cost; Iceberg: "More data files leads to more metadata stored in manifest files" and "less efficient queries from file open costs"
detection in plan or UI or event log: file count per table/partition in storage listing; input file count per stage in UI; Delta: DESCRIBE DETAIL file counts
fix: compaction: Delta OPTIMIZE ("coalescing small files into larger ones" - docs) / auto compaction; Iceberg rewriteDataFiles ("combine small files into larger files to reduce metadata overhead and runtime file open cost" - docs); write with repartition(n)/coalesce
how to measure the saving: n files before/after; scan wall time; input_bytes in event log
measured effect: 200 small files (22.3MB total): read+filter+agg 0.6s; same data as 4 compacted files (16.9MB): 0.18s (3.3x). Write side: 5.91s vs 0.43s (13.7x). [local e07]
risks: compaction rewrites data (cost); Z-order is "not idempotent" per Delta docs; old files need VACUUM/expire
prerequisites: table format tooling (Delta/Iceberg) or plain Parquet rewrite

name: missing broadcast (small dimension joined via sort-merge shuffle)
symptom: both join sides shuffle (Exchange hashpartitioning) although one side is tiny; join stage slow and shuffle-heavy
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan shows SortMergeJoin + two Exchanges when one side is a few MB; check shuffle bytes of the dim side
fix: add broadcast hint / raise spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10MB, probed); docs: BROADCAST hint "will be prioritized by Spark even if the size ... is above ... autoBroadcastJoinThreshold"
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes written + wall time, both in event log
measured effect: SMJ: 1.64s, 27.2MB shuffle; broadcast: 0.67s, 7.1MB (2.4x time, 3.8x shuffle). [local e05]
risks: broadcast of a too-large table OOMs the driver (see A06); nested-loop broadcast explodes with non-equi joins
prerequisites: dimension fits driver memory

name: oversized broadcast (forcing a big table to broadcast)
symptom: driver hangs at "Collecting broadcast" or OOMs; BroadcastExchange with huge size in plan
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan: BroadcastExchange on a table larger than threshold; driver memory spike; spark.sql.broadcastTimeout expiry
fix: do not force hints on large tables; keep threshold sane; let AQE convert SMJ->BHJ only when runtime stats say small (docs: conversion "when the runtime statistics of any join side are smaller than the adaptive broadcast hash join threshold")
how to measure the saving: driver peak memory; job success rate; broadcast build time in UI
measured effect: not measured locally (would need a deliberately oversized broadcast; risk experiment)
risks: driver OOM kills the whole job; 10MB default exists for a reason (probed value 10485760b)
prerequisites: spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold default 10MB (probed in runs/defaults_probe.txt)

name: row-at-a-time Python UDF
symptom: query hundreds of times slower than equivalent SQL; UDF black box in plan (BatchEvalPython)
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan node BatchEvalPython / !PyArrow; "operate one-row-at-a-time, and thus suffer from high serialization and invocation overhead" (Databricks)
fix: replace with built-in SQL expressions; else pandas UDF via Arrow ("3x to over 100x" faster, Databricks)
how to measure the saving: wall time of same action
measured effect: builtin 0.24s vs Python UDF 2.82s on 6M rows (11.8x). [local e06]
risks: pandas UDFs still slower than codegen SQL; UDF blocks predicate pushdown and stats
prerequisites: for Python UDF: same python version on executors (hit locally: PYSPARK_PYTHON had to be pinned)

name: collect()/toPandas() on large results
symptom: driver GC pressure, long single-threaded serialisation, OOM; rest of cluster idle
detection in plan or UI or event log: while in driver code; job stages finish then a long driver-side gap; event log shows job end followed by seconds of silence
fix: keep data distributed: write/foreach; aggregate before pulling; sample; paginate with limit
how to measure the saving: wall time collect vs write; driver heap
measured effect: 2M rows x 2 cols: collect 4.54s vs parquet write 1.18s (3.8x), plus driver holds all rows in memory. [local e12]
risks: OOM at scale; not a cluster parallel operation; single-threaded serialisation
prerequisites: result must actually be small to be safe (folklore threshold: < ~1M rows / few hundred MB)
source URL (all fetched 2026-10-17 unles: local experiment (Spark 3.5.6); folklore threshold labelled as such

name: cartesian / nested-loop join (join without usable equality)
symptom: output rows = |left| x |right|; slow join even for small inputs
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan shows BroadcastNestedLoopJoin or CartesianProduct; docs name the strategy SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL for it
fix: add the equality key to the join condition; pre-aggregate one side; rewrite as range condition with bucketed layout
how to measure the saving: wall time; output row count vs input
measured effect: row counts 500k x 500 with inequality: ~24.75M output rows in 0.55s (fast locally only because codegen; explodes combinatorially at real sizes). [local e12]
risks: row explosion is multiplicative; often a data bug (missing join key) rather than a tuning issue

name: window function without partitionBy
symptom: whole dataset moves through ONE task: no parallelism for the window computation, OOM risk on big data
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan: "Exchange SinglePartition" under Window; UI: window stage with 1 task regardless of cluster size (event log: tasks=1 with full shuffle read)
fix: add a meaningful partitionBy key; or rethink (rank over full table = order + take)
how to measure the saving: wall time; task count of the window stage
measured effect: partitioned window 2.33s (4-way shuffle 37.7MB, parallel) vs unpartitioned 2.12s but single window task reading 24MB in 1725ms (parallelism 1; the 1-task stage is the evidence, wall time hides it on 4 cores). [local e12/e01]
risks: wrong partitionBy reintroduces skew; global rank semantics must actually be needed
prerequisites: partition column with enough distinct values

name: wrapper/cast on the filter column defeats pushdown
symptom: full column decoded and filtered row-by-row although the file format could skip
detection in plan or UI or event log: pushedFilters missing in FileScan node: e.g. filter cast(k as string)='...' shows PushedFilters: [] (local plans.txt); input_bytes/records in event log far above matched rows
fix: compare literals to the column without wrapping: to_date(partition_col)=... vs partition_col=date string; note Spark 3.5 folded cast(year as int)=2023 into PartitionFilters (measured: pruned to 2M of 6M rows) - always verify in explain
how to measure the saving: input bytes + records read from event log; PushedFilters line
measured effect: D variant cast(k as string): read 27.7MB/6M rows vs plain k=: 21.7MB/3.36M rows; partition cast variant: Spark 3.5 still pruned (2M rows) - older engines/other dialects (Hive, Trino) do not. [local e10]
risks: false sense of safety: behaviour differs per engine version; always check the Scan node
prerequisites: engine with pushdown (Parquet/Delta/Iceberg)
source URL (all fetched 2026-10-17 unles: local experiment; Spark-3.5 fold verified in runs/e10_partitioning/plans.txt

name: repeated recomputation without cache
symptom: same source scanned and same derivation re-run for every action (notebooks with multiple queries on one DataFrame)
detection in plan or UI or event log: event log: repeated identical scan stages across jobs; UI: same stages reappear per query
fix: cache()/persist with explicit StorageLevel, or checkpoint for lineage cuts, or write intermediate table; unpersist after
how to measure the saving: last action times with and without; count scan stages
measured effect: dishonest simple case: parquet source + cheap expr, 3 actions: no-cache 2.67s vs cached 3.94s (cache LOSES locally - caching has a cost). With window (shuffle) lineage: 4.66s vs 5.43s (still loses on local disk; remote/slow storage changes this). [local e11/e11b]
risks: cache consumes executor memory/disk (A32 interplay); stale semantics if source changes; "Databricks recommends using automatic disk caching" over manual df.cache for their platform
prerequisites: measured on local NVMe; re-measure on the bank's real storage

name: wide select * materialisation
symptom: huge IO and storage for columns nobody reads (in views, CTAS, notebook outputs)
detection in plan or UI or event log: aggregations get automatic column pruning (measured: same 3MB read for select * into agg - Spark prunes); but WRITES/collects of select * read all columns: input_bytes in event log
fix: select only needed columns at the boundary; prune in the earliest CTE
how to measure the saving: bytes written/read; wall time
measured effect: write 3 cols 0.3s/555KB vs select * write 0.62s/2.1MB (2x time, 3.8x bytes). [local e13]
risks: pruning already handles pure aggregates - do not cargo-cult column lists inside aggregations (measured equal)

name: unnecessary repartition before write
symptom: extra full shuffle right before writing; many output files
detection in plan or UI or event log: repartition in code followed by write; event log: big shuffle stage with bytes ~= dataset size immediately before write tasks
fix: coalesce(n) (no shuffle) when only fewer files are wanted; repartition only to hit target file sizes
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes before write; file count; wall time
measured effect: repartition(200) write: 3.34s, 200 files, 28.6MB shuffled; coalesce(4): 0.39s, 4 files, no shuffle (8.6x). [local e13]
risks: coalesce squeezes into few tasks (less write parallelism at scale); repartition needed when data is skewed per partition

name: row format (CSV/JSON) for analytics tables
symptom: no predicate pushdown, no column pruning, bigger files, parsing cost
detection in plan or UI or event log: pushedFilters impossible; input_bytes ~= full file size in event log
fix: write Parquet (columnar): "Parquet is built to support very efficient compression and encoding schemes" and per-column compression (parquet.apache.org)
how to measure the saving: input bytes; wall time; on-disk size
measured effect: CSV 121MB scan+filter 1.16s vs Parquet 27MB 0.31s (3.7x); input read 121MB vs 3.8MB (pushdown + pruning). [local e08]
risks: Parquet not human-readable; schema evolution care; keep CSV for external exchange only

name: non-splittable single-file compression (gzip)
symptom: one task reads the whole file no matter the cluster; scan stage tasks=1
detection in plan or UI or event log: event log: scan stage with 1 task per file; UI shows single long task
fix: use splittable layout: snappy/zstd Parquet, or multi-block plain gzip input... practical: split at write
how to measure the saving: scan stage task count; wall time
measured effect: single 6M-row gz csv scan 5.06s vs snappy multi-file 1.75s (2.9x). [local e14]
risks: must rewrite data to fix; bzip2/zstd-parquet alternatives have different CPU costs

name: compression codec choice
symptom: bigger files -> more IO; heavier codec -> more CPU; none -> 4x size
detection in plan or UI or event log: file sizes on storage; scan time per codec
fix: per-column encodings + snappy default, zstd for cold data (Parquet docs: "compression schemes to be specified on a per-column level")
how to measure the saving: bytes on disk + scan wall time
measured effect: 2M rows: none 36.4MB/0.45s, snappy 17.1MB/0.2s, gzip 6.7MB/0.18s, zstd 5.1MB/0.15s. [local e09]
risks: gzip non-splittable (A16); zstd needs recent Spark; CPU vs IO tradeoff depends on storage bandwidth

name: missing partition design / no partition pruning
symptom: full table scan for queries touching one slice (one month etc.)
detection in plan or UI or event log: FileScan PartitionFilters: [] in explain (local plans.txt shows the pruned vs unpruned cases); input records in event log >> matched rows
fix: partitionBy low-cardinality columns (date, region); filter directly on partition columns; Iceberg hidden partitioning transforms
how to measure the saving: count input files/records/bytes before-after
measured effect: pruned year='2023': 1.12MB/2M rows read, 0.3s; unpruned: 16.5MB/2.28M rows(+row-group slop), 0.36s; at 6M rows and 3 years the gap scales linearly. [local e10]
risks: over-partitioning is the opposite failure (A19)
prerequisites: low-cardinality, query-aligned column

name: over-partitioning (high-cardinality partition column)
symptom: thousands of directories each with tiny files; metadata/listing blowup; writers emit one+ file per partition per task
detection in plan or UI or event log: file count per partition depth; driver time in file listing (job starts long before tasks)
fix: partition by coarse keys; bucket or cluster (Z-order) instead of fine partitions
how to measure the saving: count files and empty partitions before/after; listing wall time
measured effect: not measured locally (needs wide partition space; mechanism shared with A04 small files)
risks: more partitions amplify every write; ZORDER "effectiveness ... drops with each extra column" (Delta docs)

name: join key type mismatch (int vs bigint/string keys)
symptom: hidden cast on the join key: blocks bucketed joins, distorts stats-based broadcast sizing, sometimes forces extra sort
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan shows cast(...) wrapping join keys on one side; bucketed join silently degrades to shuffle
fix: cast in ETL once to a canonical type at write; align schema across tables
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes; presence of Exchange in bucketed join plan
measured effect: not measured in isolation (folded into e14 bucketing evidence: type-aligned keys needed for shuffle-free join)
risks: schema drift historically common in banks' layers (folklore, verify per repo)

name: filter applied after join/aggregation instead of before
symptom: pushdown only goes so far; big intermediate built then discarded
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan places Filter above Join although it references one side only; exchange sizes larger than necessary
fix: push filters to the earliest step (CTE order matters less in Spark than in RDBMS, but side-only filters should pre-apply)
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes; wall time
measured effect: not measured locally (labelled practice; the optimizer often does this automatically - check plan first)
risks: over-filtering can change semantics with outer joins
source URL (all fetched 2026-10-17 unles: local practice claim, flagged for verification on bank queries

name: count() as existence check
symptom: full scan to answer a yes/no
detection in plan or UI or event log: event log: full-input stage for a boolean answer
fix: filter + limit(1).count(), or EXISTS in SQL; for "any rows" checks use isEmpty()/head(1)
how to measure the saving: rows scanned (input_records)
measured effect: not measured locally (folklore, trivially true: count must touch all partitions)
risks: limit(1) races with empty partitions; semantics identical for existence

name: join used only to filter (no dim columns used)
symptom: shuffles the fact table although a semi-join would do
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan shows inner Join but target list has no columns from the right side (local e12/e05 variants demonstrate)
fix: left_semi join; Spark can also invert to a broadcast filter
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes; rows materialised in join
measured effect: not measured in isolation locally
risks: pruning depends on nullability of keys; semantics differ with duplicates

name: union/append inside a loop (many tiny jobs)
symptom: hundreds of small Spark jobs, each with startup cost; small files accumulate (compounds A04)
detection in plan or UI or event log: DAG/scheduler view: many micro jobs in the app; event log job count per notebook run
fix: batch the loop: build a list, one union at the end; or use structured streaming micro-batch
how to measure the saving: job count + wall time; files produced
measured effect: not measured locally (job-overhead dominated; visible in any bank's notebooks per folklore, verify)
risks: rewrites control flow; latency vs throughput tradeoff changes

name: build side chosen on the larger relation
symptom: driver builds a hash relation from the big side; slow broadcast build or memory churn
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan: BroadcastHashJoin BuildLeft/BuildRight on the wrong side (docs: with both sides hinted, "Spark will pick the build side based on the join type and the sizes of the relations")
fix: hint the small side with broadcast; ensure stats present so Spark sizes sides
how to measure the saving: broadcast build time; join wall time
measured effect: not measured in isolation (folded into e05: building the 200k-row side was the fast path)
risks: forcing build side wrong way OOMs; AQE re-decides from runtime stats
prerequisites: statistics present (see A27)

name: orderBy before write (unneeded global sort)
symptom: full shuffle + single-range partitioning just to produce sorted files
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan: Exchange rangepartitioning + Sort right before write
fix: sort within partitions (sortWithinPartitions) or drop the sort; rely on table clustering instead
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes; write wall time
measured effect: not measured locally (variant of A14, same mechanism)
risks: sort can serve compression (Delta stats) - removing it may hurt skipping

name: stale or missing table statistics
symptom: wrong broadcast/size decisions in the static plan; CBO disabled
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan cost rows missing or sizeInBytes absurd; ANALYZE TABLE ... COMPUTE STATISTICS output
fix: ANALYZE on key tables; or rely on AQE runtime statistics ("makes use of the runtime statistics to choose the most efficient query execution plan" - docs)
how to measure the saving: plan before/after; join strategy flips
measured effect: the static plan in e05 chose correctly only after stats/data were probed; AQE removes dependence on stale stats (blog: static sort-merge converted to broadcast at runtime)
risks: CBO in Spark is limited vs RDBMS (folklore); stats computation costs a job
prerequisites: table with stable schema

name: no bucketing for repeated big joins
symptom: every nightly job re-shuffles two huge tables on the same keys
detection in plan or UI or event log: plan: Exchange hashpartitioning on both sides of the recurring join; shuffle bytes ~= table size each run
fix: bucket both tables on the join key with matching bucket counts; SPJ configs for v2 sources; docs: "If Storage Partition Join is performed, the query plan will not contain Exchange nodes prior to the join"
how to measure the saving: shuffle bytes of the recurring join; wall time
measured effect: plain join 1.35s/27.9MB shuffle vs bucketed (8 buckets, sorted) 0.38s/0 shuffle (3.6x). [local e14]
risks: bucket count is frozen at write time; writes get slower; Databricks de-emphasises bucketing - check platform
prerequisites: writer support (saveAsTable bucketBy or table DDL)

name: executor and memory sizing
symptom: spill to disk, GC thrash, OOMs, or idle over-provisioned clusters
detection in plan or UI or event log: UI: spill (memory/disk) columns on stages; "If you observe significant spill to disk or OOM errors, increase the amount of memory" (Databricks); fewer-larger-nodes guidance: "Having fewer nodes reduces the impact of shuffles"
fix: right-size instance family; memory-optimised for shuffles; keep memory:core ratio so tasks do not spill; Databricks: "using fewer workers ... increase the size of your instances"
how to measure the saving: spill bytes in UI/event log; job wall time; cost per run
measured effect: not measured locally (single machine)
risks: Oversizing wastes money directly; undersizing spills or OOMs; JVM heap >~32GB loses compressed oops (folklore)
prerequisites: cluster manager with instance choice

name: dynamic allocation instead of fixed fleet
symptom: idle executors hold cluster money between job steps; bursty workloads overpay
detection in plan or UI or event log: event log: executor idle gaps; UI executors tab timeline
fix: enable dynamicAllocation (needs external shuffle service or shuffleTracking: docs list 4 alternatives incl. "spark.dynamicAllocation.shuffleTracking.enabled ... true"); timeouts tuned (executorIdleTimeout 60s default, folklore)
how to measure the saving: executor-hours used vs before; cost per job
measured effect: not measured locally (local[4] has no elastic pool)
risks: available on all coarse-grained cluster managers but K8s cannot use external shuffle service (docs) - use shuffle tracking; scale-up lag on bursty jobs
prerequisites: shuffle data survivable on executor removal

name: spot/preemptible capacity (cloud) vs fixed on-prem cluster
symptom: full on-demand price for interruption-tolerant batch
detection in plan or UI or event log: billing dashboard: share of on-demand spend on batch/spark jobs
fix: run Spark batch on spot with checkpointed/retryable jobs: "up to a 90% discount compared to On-Demand prices" (AWS); GCP Spot: "up to 91%" with "30 seconds to shut down"
how to measure the saving: cost per job-hour before/after; job success rate
measured effect: quoted discounts: AWS "up to 90%", GCP "up to 91%" (fetched 2026-10-17)
risks: interruptions need idempotent, restartable jobs; stragglers on reclaimed nodes; on-prem analogue is overcommit/packing instead
prerequisites: autoretry, shuffle service or shuffle tracking (A30), object-storage checkpointing

name: FinOps: unit costs and tagging
symptom: cannot answer "what does this pipeline cost per run / per TB / per business unit"
detection in plan or UI or event log: billing exports without tags; no cost-per-job view
fix: tag jobs/clusters (project, owner, data_domain); measure unit costs, e.g. BigQuery on-demand "$6.25 / 1 tebibyte" with "first 1 TiB of query data processed per month is free" (fetched 2026-10-17); FinOps: "Allocation defines how costs should be apportioned to those responsible"
how to measure the saving: establish cost per job run (compute-hours x unit price), cost per TB scanned; trend over weeks
measured effect: quoted: $6.25/TiB BigQuery on-demand; FinOps allocation quotes

name: job scheduling and dependency pruning
symptom: nightly DAG runs unchanged branches whose inputs did not move; downstream of failed branches still queued
detection in plan or UI or event log: scheduler (Airflow etc.): tasks with no new upstream data; runtime vs data-freshness gap
fix: dataset-aware scheduling / skip when input partitions unchanged (Airflow datasets, sensors on partition existence); prune unused branches
how to measure the saving: runs skipped per month x avg run cost
measured effect: not measured locally (orchestration-level)
risks: wrong freshness assumptions skip needed runs; sensors polling costs

name: duplicate pipelines computing the same result
symptom: two teams' jobs scan the same source and build the same aggregate; double cost
detection in plan or UI or event log: for each output table, find jobs writing overlapping schemas; FinOps allocation as the map ("costs should be apportioned to those responsible" - the map that exposes duplicates)
fix: one materialised owner + views/grants for consumers; query result reuse for repeated reads
how to measure the saving: count of jobs consolidated; cost delta
measured effect: before/after requires a data-lineage tool or job inventory (owner-only at the bank, see decision.md)
risks: political ownership disputes; one more moving part (the shared table)

name: result/data reuse (disk cache, materialisation)
symptom: same hot table re-fetched from object storage by every query
detection in plan or UI or event log: storage-level metrics; query latency variance cold vs warm
fix: automatic disk caching where available ("Databricks uses disk caching to speed up data reads", works "for all Parquet data files, including Delta Lake tables", "Later reads of the same data run locally and are significantly faster"); write-once intermediate tables for shared hot aggregates
how to measure the saving: cold vs warm query wall time; bytes from remote storage
measured effect: quoted (not measured here): Databricks disk-cache doc; local e11 measured manual df.cache losing on fast local disk - platform cache differs
risks: manual cache semantics (A12); disk cache is platform-specific (Databricks; OSS Spark has no equivalent enabled by default - folklore label)
prerequisites: Parquet/Delta files on slower remote storage

name: Delta/Iceberg snapshot expiry and vacuum
symptom: metadata grows forever, time-travel files never reclaimed; listing slows
detection in plan or UI or event log: describe table history: snapshot count/age (Iceberg: "Snapshots accumulate until they are expired by the expireSnapshots operation")
fix: regularly run expireSnapshots / VACUUM; Delta best practice: rewrite small files "on a regular basis" and VACUUM old files
how to measure the saving: manifest/metadata file count; snapshot age distribution; listing time
measured effect: not measured locally (needs a table with commit history)
risks: time travel window shrinks (retention compliance!); VACUUM too aggressive loses restore points
prerequisites: table-format ops available (Delta/Iceberg)

name: no clustering/Z-order for multi-predicate queries
symptom: predicate hits every file: no data skipping
detection in plan or UI or event log: Delta stats show files read per query; "co-locality is automatically used by Delta Lake in data-skipping algorithms"
fix: ZORDER/clustering on frequent predicate columns: "If you expect a column to be commonly used in query predicates and ... high cardinality ... then use ZORDER BY"
how to measure the saving: files skipped/read per query; bytes scanned
measured effect: quoted Delta Z-order guidance (fetched 2026-10-17); not measured locally (local e10 partition pruning is the single-column variant)
risks: ZORDER is "not idempotent", "effectiveness ... drops with each extra column"; wasted without column stats
prerequisites: statistics collected on the ZORDER columns

name: files.maxPartitionBytes mis-set for read parallelism
symptom: either many tiny read tasks (value too small) or fewer tasks than cores (too large)
detection in plan or UI or event log: read stage task count vs input size; default 128MB probed in runs/defaults_probe.txt
fix: tune spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes to get ~cores-many multi-hundred-MB tasks; files.openCostInBytes models per-file overhead (default 4MB, probed)
how to measure the saving: read-stage task count; wall time
measured effect: not isolated locally (e03 shows the analogous shuffle-side effect: task count 4->1000 changed wall time 1.13->2.48s)
risks: too-large tasks risk long tail/OOM; interacts with file sizes (A04)
prerequisites: splittable format (A16)

name: unaccounted executor memory overhead (YARN/K8s containers)
symptom: container killed at overhead limit although heap looks fine; "Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits" in logs
detection in plan or UI or event log: container memory requested vs heap + overhead; killed-container events
fix: factor pyspark/python worker + off-heap + netty into container sizing (practice: overhead ~10% of heap, spark.executor.memoryOverhead; folklore label)
how to measure the saving: container kill count; job success rate
measured effect: not measured locally (local mode has no container budget)
risks: too-generous overhead wastes RAM across the fleet (A29 interplay)
prerequisites: YARN/K8s deployment

name: skewed aggregation (hot groupBy key, not a join)
symptom: one reducer task aggregates the hot key; siblings idle
detection in plan or UI or event log: UI/event log: reduce stage max vs p50 task (same signal as A01 but in an aggregate stage)
fix: two-phase aggregation (partial aggregate by salted key, then merge); Spark 3.5 REBALANCE hint/partitioning (docs: skewed shuffle partitions in RebalancePartitions "split ... according to the target size")
how to measure the saving: stage max/p50 runtime; wall time
measured effect: same detection/mechanism as A01; e02 warm-up groupBy showed balanced 8-task stages after salting the join key (indirect evidence)
risks: extra shuffle for the partial pass; REBALANCE needs AQE
prerequisites: skew in grouping key, not join key

name: explode of uneven arrays concentrates rows in few tasks
symptom: post-explode stage shows straggler tasks although pre-explode data was even
detection in plan or UI or event log: event log: input_records per task vary by orders of magnitude after a Generate/explode node
fix: repartition after explode, or explode id first and join back (pattern); size-aware partitioning
how to measure the saving: task record distribution (max/p50)
measured effect: not measured locally (labelled practice; mechanism identical to A01)
risks: repartition adds shuffle; joining back adds a stage
prerequisites: array column with skewed lengths

name: event logging not enabled (no post-mortem evidence)
symptom: team cannot answer why a job was slow yesterday; UI gone after app end
detection in plan or UI or event log: no event log files in spark.eventLog.dir
fix: enable spark.eventLog.enabled (docs: "Whether to log Spark events, useful for reconstructing the Web UI after the application has finished") + shared eventLog.dir; parse JSON offline (this task's evlog parser does exactly that)
how to measure the saving: presence/size of event logs; ability to compute per-stage shuffle bytes offline
measured effect: every measurement in this catalogue came from event logs parsed by examples/common.py (summarise_eventlog)
risks: logs contain data volumes (privacy check at the bank); storage growth
prerequisites: shared writable dir (HDFS/S3) for all apps

name: shuffle-to-broadcast conversion not exploited (local shuffle reader off)
symptom: SMJ runs although one side turned out small at runtime
detection in plan or UI or event log: final plan keeps SMJ; docs: AQE converts SMJ->BHJ and "read shuffle files locally to save network traffic (provided spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled is true)"
fix: keep AQE on with localShuffleReader enabled (default true in 3.x)
how to measure the saving: final plan node types; network shuffle read bytes
measured effect: not isolated locally (AQE conversion visible in e02 final plans)
risks: conversion decisions per-query can surprise readers of plans
prerequisites: Spark 3.2+

name: reading with schema inference on every job (CSV/JSON)
symptom: each run pays a full pass just to infer schema before real work
detection in plan or UI or event log: driver-side job before the main one; event log: extra full-scan job per notebook run
fix: supply schema explicitly (read schema or schema file); convert to Parquet/Delta with fixed schema
how to measure the saving: job count; driver startup wall time
measured effect: not measured locally (folded into e08: CSV path pays parsing cost per read anyway)
risks: wrong explicit schema fails loudly (good) or truncates (strings) - test
prerequisites: types known (usually true in bank pipelines)
